designs.name: Workflow Pipeline
designs.description: A three-lane automation diagram: web, maps and AI sources on the left, a settings card in the middle, and the agents and booked confirmation they produce on the right. The elbow connectors are generated from the same coordinate table the nodes are positioned from, so every line terminates exactly on the edge it points at rather than near it. One design pixel is a fraction of the panel's own width — type, icons and toggles included — so the composition holds from a narrow masonry column to a full-width hero with no breakpoints. The toggles are drawn in a fixed state rather than wired to a handler: a still picture of a configured workflow, not a working control panel. Renders entirely on the server.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A three-lane automation diagram: web, maps and AI sources on the left, a settings card in the middle, and the agents and booked confirmation they produce on the right. Elbow connectors are generated from the same coordinate table the nodes are placed from, and every measurement is a fraction of the panel's own width, so type, icons and toggles keep their proportions at any size. Static — no hooks, no motion, zero JavaScript.

props.name: agents
props.description: The two avatar photographs in the output column, top and bottom. Each carries a sound-wave badge marking it as an agent on a call. Defaults to two Unsplash portraits served through their CDN transform at 120px.

props.name: status
props.description: Label on the middle output pill — the one result the pipeline is drawn to produce. Defaults to "Booked"; the green tick badge is part of the mark, not conditional on the text.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the panel root. The panel is aspect-ratio driven at 624/252 and fills its container's width — it is also the container-query root, so overriding its width rescales everything inside it.

designs.name: Stacked Tower
designs.description: Four cylindrical units stacked into a deliberately unsteady tower, drawn entirely from ellipses that all obey one ratio — ry = ryRatio × rx — so height is only ever vertical offset between two identical shapes, with no perspective transform, rotation or skew anywhere in the file. Each unit derives every surface it has from a single OKLCH base walked down a ramp that adds chroma and rotates hue as it darkens, which is what keeps the shadows reading as coloured light rather than as grey. Ribs are spaced evenly in angle and then projected, so they bunch toward the silhouette and start on the curve of the top ellipse the way real corrugation does. Curved leader lines are derived from the shapes themselves rather than authored beside them, so they track the geometry when it is retuned. The whole drawing is one SVG with no hooks and no runtime — it renders on the server and ships no JavaScript.

variations.name: default
variations.description: Four cylindrical units stacked into a deliberately unsteady tower. Every ellipse obeys one camera ratio, so height reads as vertical offset rather than as tilt; every surface on a unit is derived from one OKLCH base walked down a ramp that gains chroma as it darkens; ribs are spaced in angle and projected, so they bunch toward the silhouette. The base drum runs off the bottom of the card, which is what makes the tower feel taller than its frame. Static — no hooks, no motion, zero JavaScript.

props.name: geometry
props.description: Every measurement, colour and label in the drawing: the camera (ryRatio and stroke width), the shading palette (ramp, edge and contact opacities, rib step and blend), the annotation type scale and curve, the lid overhang, and the ordered list of units. Defaults to DEFAULT_GEOMETRY, which the file also exports. The one rule with no tolerance is camera.ryRatio — it applies to every ellipse at once, so changing it re-poses the whole tower, while overriding a single shape's ry would read as a tilted unit rather than a higher one.

props.name: brand
props.description: Wordmark beside the bird glyph in the masthead. Defaults to "Cardinal".

props.name: headline
props.description: Centred line under the masthead, which is also the SVG's accessible title. Defaults to "Your sales motion, built by you".

props.name: id
props.description: Prefix for every generated SVG id — the card clip, each cylinder's rib clip and edge gradient, and the title and description. SVG ids are document-global, so two instances on one page need two prefixes or the second silently steals the first's clip paths. Defaults to "stacked-tower".

props.name: className
props.description: Classes on the root <svg>. The drawing is viewBox-driven at 1230×738 with preserveAspectRatio, so it fills whatever width it is given and keeps its proportions — there are no pixel dimensions on the element.

designs.name: Notes Card
designs.description: A task list app screen, drawn inside a phone: a card that fills the display and carries its own tab bar, so the navigation belongs to the thing it navigates rather than floating beside it. Built on a design system stated once: two type pairs — 16px with medium, 14px with normal — where selection is signalled by surface and colour rather than by a third size, and letter-spacing rides on the type token so the same size is never set two ways in two components. Radii are concentric and the arithmetic is checkable: 16 on the card, 8 one padding step in, 4 two steps in. Rows are wells recessed with a 1px inset ring rather than a border, and each row ends in a rail of three action buttons whose boxes and gaps divide that rail exactly. The leading mark is a ring filled as a wedge in proportion to subtasks done, drawn on the icon set's own 24 grid at the shared stroke weight. Status pills use `text-box: trim-both cap alphabetic` to centre on their cap height rather than their line box, every control carries a 40px hit area as a pseudo-element that never overlaps its neighbour's, and transitions name the exact properties that change. Colour is OKLCH throughout at hue 264, with the ink value spent in exactly two places — the primary action and the selected tab. Renders entirely on the server.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A task list screen inside a phone shell — status bar, home indicator, and a card that fills the display between them. Header with a primary action, a segmented filter, and date-grouped rows carrying completion, status, counts and a rail of edit/complete/delete actions. Two type pairs, concentric 16/8/4 radii, 40px hit areas on every control, press feedback at 0.96, and transitions that name only the properties that move. The progress mark is a wedge drawn on the icon set's own grid, and the last row sits mid-swipe with its delete action revealed. Static — no hooks, no motion library, zero JavaScript.

props.name: time
props.description: Clock in the status bar. Defaults to "9:41". Set in tabular figures so a different time cannot shift the radios beside it.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the scaling root. The device is fixed at a 390 × 844 screen inside a 12px bezel and is scaled to the caller's width by a viewBox, so it shrinks to fit a narrow column and stops at its natural 414px — set a `max-w-*` here to cap it smaller.

designs.name: Insight Card
designs.description: A marketing card whose lower half is a halftone field with a comet swept through it — the cone is a void carved out of the dots rather than a shape drawn over them, so the sphere at its head reads as having cleared its own path. One signed-distance function decides both which dots get removed and which get thinned at the edge, so the silhouette can never drift from the wake. Dots are bucketed into three OKLCH shades by their distance from that wake, which is what gives the flat grid depth. The whole field is generated at module scope from a deterministic value hash rather than Math.random, so the server and the client draw the identical card and hydration stays quiet. The sphere is a radial gradient with its focal point pushed toward a named light azimuth, and the CTA gradient is the dot ramp dropped 0.14 in lightness so its label clears AA at both ends. Renders entirely on the server.

variations.name: default
variations.description: A marketing card whose lower half is a halftone field with a comet swept through it — the cone is a void carved out of the dots, not a shape drawn over them. One signed-distance function decides both which dots are removed and which are feathered at the edge, and three OKLCH shades bucketed by distance from the wake give the flat grid depth. Generated deterministically at module scope, so server and client draw the identical card.

props.name: brand
props.description: Wordmark beside the flower glyph, set in wide tracking. Defaults to "NORTHBEAM".

props.name: heading
props.description: The headline. A node rather than a string on purpose — the default wraps two words in font-semibold against the medium weight around them, which is the emphasis the card is composed for.

props.name: ctaLabel
props.description: Label on the gradient pill. Defaults to "Learn More"; the arrow badge is part of the mark, not conditional on the text.

props.name: href
props.description: Destination for the CTA anchor. Defaults to "#".

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the card root. The card is capped at 362px wide and lays out in fixed pixels, which is the width the halftone field, the type scale and the two-line headline break were composed against.

designs.name: Flight Card
designs.description: A full-bleed travel poster with the flight held behind a progressive blur that fades away at the card's midline — airport codes, cities and times either side of an airplane on a dashed route track, with the duration beneath it. The painted sky under the photograph doubles as a grade over it, so a photograph the component never chose still belongs to the card. Colour is OKLCH throughout, every fade is an eased gradient rather than a linear one, and the frame and its controls carry separate concentric radius systems. Every measurement is a fraction of the card's own width — blur radius, dash rhythm and icon included — so it holds its composition from a narrow column to a full-width hero with no breakpoints. Renders entirely on the server.

props.name: image
props.description: Background photograph. Defaults to a San Francisco bridge from Pexels, served through their CDN transform (287KB rather than the 4.0MB original). Pass your own URL to own the asset, or "" to fall through to the painted sky alone — every text pair on the card is measured to pass APCA Lc 60 against either.

props.name: from
props.description: Origin as { code, time, city }. Defaults to LHR / 10:30 AM / London.

props.name: to
props.description: Arrival as { code, time, city }. Defaults to SFO / 1:20 PM / San Francisco.

props.name: duration
props.description: Time in the air, shown under the route mark — the one number that makes two clock times mean something. Written, not computed: the endpoint times are display strings in unknown timezones. Defaults to "10h 50m".

props.name: grade
props.description: How hard the card's palette is pushed onto the photograph, using the same sky gradient the card falls back to. "tone" (default) is a soft-light pass that keeps the photo's own hues — chroma survives at 98% — and unifies its tone; "duotone" is a colour pass that imposes the palette completely at no contrast cost, but flattens vivid colour to about 55% chroma; "none" leaves the photo alone. Ignored when there is no image.

props.name: options
props.description: The two labels in the segment control. Drawn, not wired — this is a still card, so the control shows a choice rather than offering one.

props.name: activeOption
props.description: Which of the two reads as chosen. Defaults to 0, so the chosen segment agrees with the artwork and the route.

props.name: className
props.description: Additional classes on the card root. The card is aspect-ratio driven at 3:4 and fills its container's width.
